title: ESP tests in a Faraday cage at the Round Table

tellings.quote: built a Faraday cage there and I think you know, was one of the first people as far as I understand doing ESP tests in a in a Faraday cage

plain: In the early 1950s, at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, a researcher is said to have built a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electric and radio signals, and run tests of ESP, the claimed ability to sense or send information by mind alone, inside it. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this from his own understanding, without naming a source, calling it one of the first such tests "in a Faraday cage." The point of the cage was to rule out ordinary radio signals as the way any information got through.
